arxiv-2101-11907.title: The fraud loss for selecting the model complexity in fraud detection
arxiv-2101-11907.creator: Simon Boge Brant, Ingrid Hobæk Haff
arxiv-2101-11907.description: Abstract In fraud detection applications, the investigator is typically limited to controlling a restricted number k k of cases. The most efficient manner of allocating the resources is then to try selecting the k k cases with the highest probability of being fraudulent.

arxiv-2106-03730.title: Encouraging Neural Machine Translation to Satisfy Terminology Constraints
arxiv-2106-03730.creator: Melissa Ailem, Jinghsu Liu, Raheel Qader
arxiv-2106-03730.description: Abstract We present a new approach to encourage neural machine translation to satisfy lexical constraints. Our method acts at the training step and thereby avoiding the introduction of any extra computational overhead at inference step. The proposed method combines three main ingredients. The first one consists in augmenting the training data to specify the constraints.

arxiv-2107-07818.title: Revisiting IoT Device Identification PubID: pubid: 978-3-903176-40-9 ©2021 Crown
arxiv-2107-07818.creator: Roman Kolcun, Diana Andreea Popescu, Vadim Safronov, Poonam Yadav, Anna Maria Mandalari, Richard Mortier, Hamed Haddadi
arxiv-2107-07818.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Roman Kolcun, Diana Andreea Popescu, Vadim Safronov, Poonam Yadav, Anna Maria Mandalari, Richard Mortier, Hamed Haddadi. Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices are known to be the source of many security problems, and as such, they would greatly benefit from automated management. This requires robustly identifying devices so that appropriate network security policies can be applied. We address this challenge by exploring how to accurately identify IoT devices based on their network behavior, while leveraging approaches previously proposed by other researchers.

arxiv-2112-00224.title: Functional regression clustering
arxiv-2112-00224.creator: Susana Conde, Shahin Tavakoli, Daphne Ezer
arxiv-2112-00224.description: Abstract Gene expression data is often collected in time series experiments, under different experimental conditions. There may be genes that have very different gene expression profiles over time, but that adjust their gene expression patterns in the same way under experimental conditions.

arxiv-2112-03849.title: Natural Answer Generation: From Factoid Answer to Full-length Answer using Grammar Correction
arxiv-2112-03849.creator: Manas Jain, Sriparna Saha, Pushpak Bhattacharyya, Gladvin Chinnadurai, Manish Kumar Vatsa
arxiv-2112-03849.description: Abstract Question Answering systems these days typically use template-based language generation. Though adequate for a domain-specific task, these systems are too restrictive and predefined for domain-independent systems. This paper proposes a system that outputs a full-length answer given a question and the extracted factoid answer (short spans such as named entities) as the input.

arxiv-2207-12842.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Video Transformers in Action Recognition
arxiv-2207-12842.creator: Victor G. Turrisi da Costa, Giacomo Zara, Paolo Rota, Thiago Oliveira-Santos, Nicu Sebe, Vittorio Murino, Elisa Ricci
arxiv-2207-12842.description: Abstract Over the last few years, Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) techniques have acquired remarkable importance and popularity in computer vision. However, when compared to the extensive literature available for images, the field of videos is still relatively unexplored. On the other hand, the performance of a model in action recognition is heavily affected by domain shift.

arxiv-2308-04991.title: Rejuvenation and memory effects in active glasses induced by thermal and active cycling
arxiv-2308-04991.creator: Giulia Janzen, Liesbeth M. C. Janssen
arxiv-2308-04991.description: Abstract It has recently been shown that thermal active glasses can display physical aging behavior comparable to that of passive glasses, although there are some notable distinctions due to the intrinsic non-equilibrium nature of active matter. The question whether active disordered materials can also exhibit rejuvenation and memory effects, akin to the phenomenology of e.g.

arxiv-2311-10747.title: Safety-aware Causal Representation for Trustworthy Offline Reinforcement Learning in Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2311-10747.creator: Haohong Lin, Wenhao Ding, Zuxin Liu, Yaru Niu, Jiacheng Zhu, Yuming Niu, Ding Zhao
arxiv-2311-10747.description: Abstract In the domain of autonomous driving, the offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) approaches exhibit notable efficacy in addressing sequential decision-making problems from offline datasets. However, maintaining safety in diverse safety-critical scenarios remains a significant challenge due to long-tailed and unforeseen scenarios absent from offline datasets.

arxiv-2401-03646.title: Evaluating Brain-Inspired Modular Training in Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
arxiv-2401-03646.creator: Jatin Nainani
arxiv-2401-03646.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have experienced a rapid rise in AI, changing a wide range of applications with their advanced capabilities. As these models become increasingly integral to decision-making, the need for thorough interpretability has never been more critical. Mechanistic Interpretability offers a pathway to this understanding by identifying and analyzing specific sub-networks or ’circuits’ within these complex systems.

arxiv-2406-04086.title: A Survey of Language-Based Communication in Robotics
arxiv-2406-04086.creator: William Hunt W.Hunt@soton.ac.uk
arxiv-2406-04086.description: Abstract Embodied robots which can interact with their environment and neighbours are increasingly being used as a test case to develop Artificial Intelligence. This creates a need for multimodal robot controllers that can operate across different types of information, including text.

arxiv-2511-11355.title: Model Class Selection
arxiv-2511-11355.creator: Ryan Cecil, Lucas Mentch Department of Statistics, University of Pittsburgh
arxiv-2511-11355.description: Abstract Classical model selection seeks to find a single model within a particular class that optimizes some pre-specified criteria, such as maximizing a likelihood or minimizing a risk. More recently, there has been an increased interest in model set selection (MSS), where the aim is to identify a (confidence) set of near-optimal models.

pmc-10738730.title: TRANSITIONS TO LIVING ALONE AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING OF OLDER ADULTS IN THE U.S: ARE THERE ANY RACE DISPARITIES?
pmc-10738730.creator: Wuyi Dong, Qian Song
pmc-10738730.description: We extend the existing literature on living alone and psychological well-being in older adults by focusing on the transition process from other living arrangements to living alone. We examine how transitioning to living alone is associated with psychological well-being scores (measured by 21-item Ryff Measures of Psychological Well-being) and how the associations vary across racial and ethnic groups.

pmc-11470961.title: Nb1.60Ti0.32W0.08O5−δ as negative electrode active material for durable and fast-charging all-solid-state Li-ion batteries
pmc-11470961.creator: Chanho Kim, Gyutae Nam, Yoojin Ahn, Xueyu Hu, Meilin Liu
pmc-11470961.description: Li-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are considered feasible candidates for the development of the next generation of high-energy rechargeable batteries. However, ASSBs are detrimentally affected by a limited rate capability and inadequate performance at high currents. To circumvent these issues, here we propose the use of Nb1.60Ti0.32W0.08O5-δ (NTWO) as negative electrode active material.

pmc-12575948.description: This study planned to assess the prevalence and associated factor of perceived stigma among caregiver of patient with mental illness in Ethiopia. pmc-13032208.title: Age-specific clinical profiles and economic burden of pediatric tuberculosis: a 5-year retrospective study in central China
pmc-13032208.creator: Xiaojun Wang, Cuili Yang, Meilan Zhou, Cuiping Xiao, Xiaolu Yu, Qian Fu
pmc-13032208.description: BackgroundResearch on the economic burden of pediatric tuberculosis (TB) remains scarce. This study aims to investigate the hospitalization characteristics, direct medical expenses, and key determinants of hospitalization costs in pediatric TB patients.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective analysis of the hospitalization information system of a tertiary specialized tuberculosis hospital in Hubei Province, China.

pmc-13348222.title: Coding complete genome of LPAI H16N3 virus from Australia suggests intercontinental movement
pmc-13348222.creator: Nicole Brook, Simon Hollamby, Matthew Neave, Vittoria Stevens, Michelle Wille
pmc-13348222.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Herein, we report on the second low pathogenicity avian influenza (LPAI) H16N3 genome sequenced in Oceania. Revealing the viral diversity in Australia’s wild bird reservoir, including in gulls, is critical to the preparation for the arrival of HPAI H5N1. ANNOUNCEMENT

Surveillance for avian influenza viruses (AIV) (species: Alphainfluenzavirus influenzae, Family: Orthomyxoviridae) in wild birds is crucial to better understand the ecology and evolution of these viruses and continue to confirm the absence of high-pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1.

pmc-13591903.title: Small-sided games as an integrated training strategy: effects on aerobic endurance and passing performance in adolescent soccer players – a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13591903.creator: Sinan Seyhan, Furkan Can Gündüz, Görkem Açar, Fatma Gözlükaya Girginer, Çağlar Soylu, Yunus Emre Aslan, Muhammed Fatih Bilici
pmc-13591903.description: BackgroundSmall-sided games (SSG) are increasingly used in youth soccer training because they simultaneously expose players to physiological, technical, and perceptual–cognitive demands similar to competitive match play. However, evidence regarding their combined effects on aerobic endurance and passing performance in adolescent players remains limited.

pmc-13665655.title: A Comprehensive Toolkit to Support Self‐Report Questionnaires for Autistic Adults With Cognitive Disability
pmc-13665655.creator: Vicky Caron, Isabelle Courcy, Isabelle Soulières
pmc-13665655.description: ObjectivesAutistic individuals with cognitive disability are underrepresented in research using self‐report measures. This study aimed to develop a toolkit of customizable accommodations to facilitate self‐report and to explore its usability through implementation with quality of life (QoL) questionnaires.MethodsA consultation process in three rounds was conducted with 10 experts in autism and/or cognitive disability to identify accommodations.

uslaw-usc-t34-s10643.description: United States Code, Title 34 (Crime Control And Law Enforcement); Chapter 101 (Justice System Improvement); Subchapter XXXII (Crime Free Rural State Grants). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general A statewide strategic prevention plan shall be used by the rural State to assist local communities, both directly and through existing State programs and services, in building comprehensive, strategic, and innovative approaches.

uslaw-usc-t51-s71104.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t51-s71104.description: United States Code, Title 51 (National And Commercial Space Programs); Chapter 711 (Near-Earth Objects). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Administrator shall maintain a planetary radar that is comparable to the capability provided through the Deep Space Network Goldstone facility of the Administration.
